evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The current `manager_restarted` check only requires nonempty, different manager PIDs and invocation IDs. An unexpected guest reboot between the two snapshots can produce exactly those differences, so the check can report an isolated manager restart when the observations actually span a reboot. The snapshot structure already carries `boot_id` (used for the reboot check), so requiring nonempty, equal manager-snapshot boot IDs while retaining the PID and invocation-ID checks is the smallest correctness fix, not a new external requirement.
